newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE BRENT MUST BATTLE RESISTANCE TO MOVE UP.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE BRENT MUST BATTLE RESISTANCE TO MOVE UP.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* A long term return to $20.50 could be on the cards for IPE Brent. Stiff resistance around $18.85 must be broken to go higher.
* Gas oil has limited upside potential today but this is capped around $172.50, the bottom of a gap down from late last week.

IPE Brent crude and gas oil prices are seen continuing to move higher following Tuesday's bullish action, but both contracts must do battle with some stiff resistance in order to get to the higher ground, analysts said.

On Tuesday Brent gapped well above short term support around $18.40 on the opening and closed around the day's high at $18.85 after taking out the $18.80 barrier, which represented a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of last weeks price fall.
Independent analyst Elli Gifford said, "I think this market has seen its low. But there is a considerable amount of resistance around $18.85."
That included several Fibonacci extensions and retracements to get through to go higher, she said.
"But I think in the long term the market will overcome these and a return to $20.50 could be on the cards," she added.

Past $18.85 there is little upside resistance. Analysts said the psychological $19 barrier may provide initial resistance but then there is little in the way until around $19.40 where previous trendline support from July 15 to August 6 on the spot month chart may now provide a barrier.
From there $19.64, the level where the previous rally broke down beckons and then $20.50 comes into view.

Al Graham at Elliott Wave international was less convinced of the market's strengths. "Prices would have to breach the $19.12ish zone in an impulsive manner today to open up the door to $19.64, and that is low probability".

Support, stemming from last Fridays low and parallel to the previous uptrend, comes in at around $18.50-55 and below this technical weight is also being provided by dynamic support on the spot month continuation chart stemming from June 11's $17.32 extending up through July 15's $17.80 low.
That comes in today at around $18.40.

14-day RSI's stand in neutral territory and there is little sign of a bearish convergence on the 10 and 20 moving average lines. Slow stochastics lines on the September chart are on the point of crossing but at this lower level are likely to point the market higher again.
Gas oil has limited upside potential today but this is capped around $172.50, the bottom of the gap down from last Thursday and Friday's price action, unless the gap is filled.
"I think the market will fill this gap in the long term and we should then get back to trade on higher ground," Gifford said.
The down side is also limited to with RSI's back in oversold territory and trendline support parallel to the rise from July 15 coming in at around $170 today.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
